pre.validation.description: Validates incoming HL7 messages against defined rules. Use step-level controls (Required + Error Strategy) to control whether validation failures stop the pipeline (NACK) or continue with warnings (ACK).
useCases: Critical validation (Required=true): Patient safety fields → NACK on failure, stop pipeline
Data quality monitoring (Required=false + Error Strategy=continue): Accept with warnings → ACK, continue pipeline
Skip validation (Enabled=false): Emergency bypass → Skip all checks
Validate field formats (dates, numeric values, coded values)
Enforce business rules (age ranges, allowed codes, required fields)

rules.errorMessage: Birth date must be YYYYMMDD format
Patient class must be I, O, or E

parameters.name: field
parameters.description: JSONPath to the field in parsed HL7 message. Use field selector autocomplete to choose from available fields. Examples: "enhancedSegments.PID.fields[0].value" for Patient ID, "enhancedSegments.PID.fields[1].subfields[0].value" for Family Name (atomic subfield).

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: Validation type to apply. Available types: "required" (field must have a value), "format" (value must match regex pattern), "range" (numeric value within min/max), "length" (string length constraints), "enum" (value must be in allowed list), "date" (valid date format), "custom" (custom JavaScript validation).

parameters.name: errorMessage
parameters.description: Human-readable error message displayed when validation fails. Auto-populated based on field and validation type, but can be customized. Example: "Patient ID is required" or "Birth date must be YYYYMMDD format".

parameters.name: pattern
parameters.description: Regular expression pattern for "format" validation type. Example: "^\d{8}$" for 8-digit date, "^[A-Z]{2}\d{5}$" for 2 letters + 5 digits.

parameters.name: minLength / maxLength
parameters.description: String length constraints for "length" validation type. Example: minLength=1, maxLength=100 for patient name.

parameters.name: min / max
parameters.description: Numeric value range for "range" validation type. Example: min=0, max=120 for patient age.

parameters.name: allowedValues
parameters.description: List of allowed values for "enum" validation type. Example: ["M", "F", "U"] for administrative sex.

parameters.name: customScript
parameters.description: Custom JavaScript function for "custom" validation type. Function receives field value and returns true/false. Example: "function(value) { return new Date(value) > new Date('1900-01-01'); }"

validationTypes.description: Field must have a non-empty value
validationTypes.usedFor: Ensuring critical fields like Patient ID, Message Type, or Date of Birth are present

validationTypes.description: Field value must match a regular expression pattern
validationTypes.usedFor: Validating date formats, ID patterns, phone numbers, postal codes

validationTypes.description: String length must be within specified min/max range
validationTypes.usedFor: Enforcing name length limits, comment field constraints

validationTypes.description: Numeric value must be within specified min/max range
validationTypes.usedFor: Validating lab values, patient age, vital signs

validationTypes.description: Field value must be one of the allowed values

example.errorMessage: Sex must be M, F, U, or O

validationTypes.usedFor: Validating coded values like gender, patient class, result status

validationTypes.description: Field must be a valid date in specified format
validationTypes.usedFor: Validating birth dates, admission dates, observation timestamps

example.customScript: function(value) { const age = (Date.now() - new Date(value)) / 31557600000; return age >= 0 && age <= 120; }

validationTypes.usedFor: Complex business rules, cross-field validation, calculated validations

pre.logic.switch.description: Routes messages through different processing paths based on field value matching. Evaluates a single field against multiple case values and executes corresponding actions. Supports multi-step routing where a single case can trigger a sequence of steps to execute in order. Ideal for message type routing, status-based processing, and complex multi-branch conditional workflows.
useCases: Route messages by type (ADT^A01 → admission flow, ADT^A03 → discharge flow, ORU^R01 → lab flow)
Process by patient class (I → inpatient enrichment, O → outpatient enrichment, E → emergency fast-track)
Handle status codes (A → active processing, C → cancelled cleanup, P → pending queue)
Route by facility (FAC001 → Epic integration, FAC002 → Cerner integration, FAC003 → custom flow)
Process by priority (STAT → immediate, ROUTINE → normal queue, ASAP → expedited)
Branch by insurance type (MEDICARE → CMS validation, MEDICAID → state rules, COMMERCIAL → standard)
Multi-step workflows (ADT^A01 → [Validate Patient, Enrich Demographics, Route to ADT Handler])
Skip specific steps for certain cases (ORU^R01 → skip patient enrichment, go directly to lab processing)

example.description: Route by message type with multi-step execution

parameters.name: field
parameters.description: HL7 field path to evaluate. Use the field selector to choose from available fields. Examples: "MSH.9.1" for message type code, "PV1.2" for patient class, "PID.8" for gender.

parameters.name: cases
parameters.description: Array of case definitions. Each case has a value to match and actions to execute when matched. Cases are evaluated in order; first match wins.

parameters.name: cases[].value
parameters.description: The value to match against the field. Exact match by default (use options.caseInsensitive for case-insensitive matching).

parameters.name: cases[].label
parameters.description: Human-readable label for this case. Displayed in the UI for documentation purposes.

parameters.name: cases[].actions
parameters.description: Actions to execute when this case matches. Multiple actions can be defined and execute in order.

parameters.name: default
parameters.description: Fallback configuration when no cases match. Contains actions array.

parameters.name: default.actions
parameters.description: Actions to execute when no cases match. Typically "continue" or error handling.

parameters.name: options.caseInsensitive
parameters.description: Perform case-insensitive value matching. Default: false. Set to true for values like "M"/"m" or "STAT"/"stat".

parameters.name: options.trimWhitespace
parameters.description: Trim leading/trailing whitespace before comparison. Default: true. Handles HL7 padding automatically.

actions.description: Continue to the next step in sequence
actions.usedFor: Normal flow - process continues to the next step based on sequence number
Halting processing for invalid/unsupported message types, or when no further processing needed

actions.description: Set a field value in the message data
actions.usedFor: Tagging messages with category, routing metadata, or computed values
actions.parameters: targetField (where to set), value (what to set)

actions.description: Copy value from one field to another
actions.usedFor: Duplicating field values, creating backup copies, or preparing data for downstream steps

actions.description: Apply a transformation to a field value
actions.usedFor: Formatting field values - uppercase, lowercase, trim, capitalize, substring

actions.description: Route to one or more specific steps by ID
actions.usedFor: Branching to different processing paths. Supports multi-step routing for complex workflows.
actions.parameters: targetStepId (single step) OR targetStepIds (array of steps to execute in order)

actions.usedFor: Bypassing steps that are not relevant for this case (e.g., skip patient enrichment for lab messages)
actions.parameters: skipStepIds (array of step IDs to skip)

multiStepRouting.title: Multi-Step Routing
multiStepRouting.description: A single case can route to multiple steps that execute in sequence. This enables complex workflows where one condition triggers a chain of processing steps.
howToUse: In the Configuration tab, select a case
Use the dropdown to add multiple target steps
Steps are displayed as numbered chips (1. Step A, 2. Step B, etc.)
Click × on any chip to remove a step from the sequence

example.scenario: ADT messages need validation, enrichment, then specialized handling
example.execution: validate-patient runs first, then enrich-demographics, then adt-handler

comparisonWithIfThenElse.title: Switch/Case vs If-Then-Else
comparisonWithIfThenElse.description: Both steps support conditional logic but are optimized for different scenarios:

comparison.switchCase: Single field with multiple possible values
comparison.ifThenElse: Complex conditions with multiple fields and operators
Any comparison (equals, contains, greater than, less than, regex, is_empty)
If patient age > 65 AND has chronic condition, flag high-risk

comparisonWithIfThenElse.recommendation: Use Switch/Case when you have a single field with many possible values (like message type, patient class, facility code). Use If-Then-Else when you need complex boolean logic combining multiple conditions.

bestPractices.practice: Use meaningful case labels
bestPractices.reason: Labels make the configuration self-documenting and easier to maintain
bestPractices.example: Label "Admission" for value "ADT^A01" instead of leaving blank

bestPractices.practice: Always define a default case
bestPractices.reason: Handles unexpected values gracefully instead of silent failures
bestPractices.example: Default: log warning + continue, or route to error handler

bestPractices.practice: Use caseInsensitive for user-entered data
bestPractices.reason: HL7 data may have inconsistent casing (e.g., "M" vs "m" for male)
bestPractices.example: Enable caseInsensitive for PID.8 (gender), PV1.2 (patient class)

bestPractices.practice: Keep actions simple per case
bestPractices.reason: Complex logic should be in dedicated steps, not crammed into switch actions
bestPractices.example: Use route_to_step to branch to specialized processing steps rather than multiple set_value actions

bestPractices.practice: Test with edge cases
bestPractices.reason: Empty values, null fields, and whitespace can cause unexpected matching
bestPractices.example: Test with empty MSH.9, whitespace-padded values, and unexpected message types

troubleshooting.issue: Case not matching expected value
troubleshooting.cause: Whitespace in field value, case sensitivity mismatch, or wrong field path
troubleshooting.fix: Enable trimWhitespace option (default), enable caseInsensitive option if needed, and verify field path using field selector

troubleshooting.issue: Default case always executing
troubleshooting.cause: Field path returns null/undefined, no cases defined, or field value has unexpected format
troubleshooting.fix: Check field path is correct using field selector, add case definitions, and use test message to verify actual field values

troubleshooting.issue: Multi-step routing not executing all steps
troubleshooting.cause: Step IDs are incorrect, target steps are disabled, or an earlier step has a stop action
troubleshooting.fix: Verify step IDs match exactly (case-sensitive), check that target steps are enabled, and review step configurations for stop actions

troubleshooting.issue: Actions not being applied
troubleshooting.cause: Wrong action type selected, missing required parameters, or target field path invalid
troubleshooting.fix: Verify action type matches your intent, ensure all required parameters are filled (e.g., targetField for set_value), and check field paths are valid

if_then_else.description: Conditional branching step (services/executors/control/conditional_executor.go, "If-Then-Else" v2.0.0). Evaluates one or more independent {field, operator, value} conditions in order and runs the matching onTrue/onFalse action(s) for each. Uses the same shared operator evaluator as Switch/Case and hl7.build's per-segment/field conditions (services/executors/condition.go) — 12 operators, cross-field comparisons via compareToField, not just literal-value matching. If ANY condition evaluates true, the step's overall branch is "true" and the pipeline auto-skips the false branch's steps (and vice versa) via _routing.branchTaken — no manual skip_steps needed for a simple two-branch flow. See pre.logic.switch's own documentation for a side-by-side comparison of when to use which.
useCases: Flag a patient as high-risk when age > 65 AND a chronic-condition field is set — chained conditions a single-field Switch/Case can't express
Reject a message outright (action: "reject") when a required cross-field relationship is violated, e.g. discharge date before admission date
Route to a specific downstream step only when a field is missing (operator: "not_exists") without needing a Switch/Case default case
Compare two fields against each other (compareToField) rather than a field against a literal — e.g. flag when PV1.44 (admission) is later than PV1.45 (discharge)
Tag metadata (set_metadata) for later steps to read, without altering the message body itself

parameters.name: conditions
parameters.description: One or more independent condition blocks, evaluated in order: {name, condition, onTrue, onFalse}. Every condition in the array is evaluated and its matching branch's actions run — this is not a first-match-wins list like Switch/Case's cases.

parameters.name: conditions[].condition
parameters.description: {field, operator, value, compareToField}. field is the path to evaluate; operator is one of equals, not_equals, contains, starts_with, ends_with, greater_than, greater_than_or_equal, less_than, less_than_or_equal, exists, not_exists, regex_match, in_list (services/executors/condition.go — the same evaluator Switch/Case and hl7.build's conditions use). value is the literal to compare against (unused/optional for exists/not_exists). compareToField, when set, compares against another field's current value instead of the literal value.

parameters.name: conditions[].onTrue / conditions[].onFalse
parameters.description: The action(s) to run for that branch. Accepts either a single action object ({action: "..."}) or an array of action objects — both are supported; use an array when a branch needs more than one action.

actions.usedFor: The branch that needs no side effect.

actions.description: Fails the message with an error, stopping the pipeline for it.
actions.usedFor: Hard validation failures that must NACK/stop rather than continue.

actions.parameters: message, continue (bool, default true — set false to stop processing after the warning)
message, continue (bool, default FALSE — unlike log_warning, this stops processing by default unless continue:true is set explicitly)

actions.description: Merges keys into the message's _metadata object.
actions.usedFor: Tagging for later steps/reporting without touching the message body.
actions.parameters: metadata (object of key/value pairs to merge)

actions.description: Sets a routing destination/queue and/or a single conditional next step.
actions.usedFor: Lower-level routing distinct from route_to_step — sets _routing.destination/.queue directly.

actions.description: Sets a field value on the message.
actions.usedFor: Writing a computed/flag value onto the message for downstream steps.
actions.parameters: field (target path), value — NOT targetField; see the troubleshooting entry below, this differs from Switch/Case's own set_value action.

actions.description: Copies one field's value to another.
actions.usedFor: Duplicating a value onto a normalized field name.
actions.parameters: source, target — NOT sourceField/targetField; see the troubleshooting entry below, this differs from Switch/Case's own copy_field action.

actions.description: Removes a field from the message.
actions.usedFor: Stripping a field once it's no longer needed downstream.

actions.description: Routes to one or more specific steps by ID, same multi-step mechanism Switch/Case uses.
actions.parameters: stepId (or targetStepId) for a single step, OR targetStepIds (array) for multiple in order; optional skipSteps (array) to force the OTHER branch's steps to be skipped even if they weren't auto-excluded — see the exclusive-branch note in Best Practices.

bestPractices.practice: Every condition in the array is evaluated — this is not first-match-wins
bestPractices.reason: Unlike Switch/Case's cases (first match wins), all of if_then_else's conditions run and each one's matching branch executes. Two conditions that are both true both fire their onTrue actions.
bestPractices.example: Two independent checks (age > 65, AND separately has-chronic-condition) — both conditions run and both can tag metadata, even though neither one "wins" over the other.

bestPractices.practice: Only the LAST routing action across all conditions actually takes effect
bestPractices.reason: route_to_step/route_to actions are collected and executed once, after every condition has run — if more than one condition's branch calls a routing action, only the final one encountered is applied; earlier ones are silently overwritten, not combined.
bestPractices.example: If both Condition 1's onTrue and Condition 2's onFalse call route_to_step, only Condition 2's routing is the one that actually executes.

bestPractices.practice: Let branchTaken handle simple two-branch exclusion; use skipSteps only for more complex cases
bestPractices.reason: _routing.branchTaken ("true"/"false") is set automatically from whether ANY condition matched, and the pipeline already uses it to skip the other branch's steps for a straightforward if/else — route_to_step's own skipSteps parameter exists for cases branchTaken's simple true/false split can't express (e.g. multiple independent conditions with different step sets to exclude).
bestPractices.example: A single condition with a true-path step and a false-path step needs no skipSteps at all — branchTaken already excludes the untaken path.

troubleshooting.issue: set_value/set_field action runs without error but the field never actually updates
troubleshooting.cause: If-Then-Else's set_field/set_value action reads its target from the "field" key — a config written for (or copied from) a Switch/Case case, which uses "targetField" for the same action name, is silently ignored here since "targetField" isn't a key this action reads.
troubleshooting.fix: Use {"action": "set_field", "field": "message.yourField", "value": "..."} — "field", not "targetField".

troubleshooting.issue: copy_field silently copies nothing
troubleshooting.cause: Same class of gotcha as set_field — this action reads "source"/"target", not Switch/Case's "sourceField"/"targetField".
troubleshooting.fix: Use {"action": "copy_field", "source": "message.a", "target": "message.b"}.

troubleshooting.issue: Only one of two conditions' routing actions seems to run
troubleshooting.cause: Not a bug — see the Best Practices entry above: only the last routing action across ALL conditions in the array is executed, by design (routing is deferred and applied once, after every condition has been evaluated).
troubleshooting.fix: Keep at most one condition emitting a routing action, or order conditions so the one you want to win is evaluated last.

troubleshooting.issue: "condition is required" error even though conditions look correctly configured
troubleshooting.cause: The executor accepts three config shapes for backward compatibility (newest: conditions[] array; newer: ifThenElse.conditions; legacy: a single top-level condition/then_actions/else_actions) — a config with the array present but each entry missing its own nested "condition" object still fails, since each array entry needs {name, condition, onTrue, onFalse}, not a flat condition at the array level.
troubleshooting.fix: Confirm each entry in conditions[] has its own nested condition object: {name: "...", condition: {field, operator, value}, onTrue: {...}, onFalse: {...}}.

pre.enrichment.api.description: Enriches HL7 messages by querying external REST APIs (EMPI, EHR, LIMS, insurance systems). Supports all authentication methods including OAuth 2.0 with automatic token management. 100% Postman feature parity.
useCases: Epic FHIR EMPI lookup - Get complete patient demographics using MRN
Cerner EMPI - Retrieve patient master index data with OAuth 2.0

bestPractices.practice: Always test queries first
bestPractices.reason: Query Tester shows real results and prevents SQL errors in production
bestPractices.example: Run test query with sample MRN before deploying pipeline

bestPractices.practice: Use named connection strings (future)

bestPractices.practice: Limit result rows in query
bestPractices.reason: Prevents performance issues from large result sets
bestPractices.example: Add LIMIT 1 to queries that should return single row (patient lookup, provider lookup)

bestPractices.practice: Use specific column names
bestPractices.reason: SELECT * causes issues when schema changes. Specify exact columns needed.
bestPractices.example: Use SELECT id, name, mrn instead of SELECT *

bestPractices.practice: Set appropriate timeout
bestPractices.reason: Balance between allowing slow queries and preventing pipeline hangs
bestPractices.example: Simple lookups: 1000ms, complex joins: 5000ms, reporting queries: 10000ms

bestPractices.practice: Use failOnError wisely
bestPractices.reason: Critical enrichment should fail pipeline; optional enrichment should continue
bestPractices.example: EMPI lookup (critical): failOnError=true, Provider specialty (nice-to-have): failOnError=false

pre.enrichment.script.description: Execute custom JavaScript logic to calculate, transform, or enrich data from HL7 messages and previous enrichment steps. Use this for complex business rules, risk scoring, data validation, custom calculations, and conditional logic that cannot be achieved through simple mappings. Results are stored in enriched_data and can be referenced by subsequent steps.
useCases: Calculate patient risk scores based on age, diagnoses, and lab values
Determine insurance eligibility by combining patient demographics with external data
Perform complex date calculations (e.g., days since last admission, appointment intervals)
Apply business rules for message routing or prioritization
Validate and transform data formats (e.g., normalize phone numbers, format addresses)
Enrich data by combining HL7 fields with database/API results from previous steps
Generate derived fields (e.g., BMI from height/weight, age from date of birth)
Implement conditional logic for data transformation (if-then-else scenarios)

parameters.description: JavaScript code to execute. The script receives the input object containing HL7 message and enriched data from previous steps. Must return an object with calculated/enriched fields.

parameters.name: timeout_ms
parameters.description: Maximum execution time in milliseconds (default: 5000). Script will be terminated if it exceeds this limit.

parameters.name: failOnError
parameters.description: Whether to fail the entire pipeline if script execution fails (default: false). Set to true for critical calculations.

examples.explanation: Use getHL7Field(input, "segment.field") to extract values from the HL7 message
Use getNestedValue(input, xpath) to access data from previous database enrichment steps
Access data returned from API calls in previous enrichment steps
Access metadata fields added by the metadata enrichment step

examples.code: return { riskScore: 9, riskLevel: "moderate", calculatedAt: new Date().toISOString() };
examples.explanation: Return an object with calculated fields. These will be stored in ["Script_Enrichment"].enriched_data and available to subsequent steps including field mapping.

bestPractices.recommendation: Always validate input data before performing calculations to avoid runtime errors
bestPractices.example: if (chronicConditions && chronicConditions > 0) { /* safe to use */ }

bestPractices.recommendation: Keep scripts lightweight and avoid complex loops. Use database/API enrichment for heavy data operations.

post.validation.description: Validates FHIR data against the R4 specification. Works in two modes: Bundle mode (validates bundle structure + all entry resources) when fhirBundle contains a Bundle, and Resource mode (validates a single standalone resource) when fhirResource is present or fhirBundle contains a non-Bundle resource. Searches fhirBundle, fhirResource, message.*, and enriched.*.
useCases: Validate FHIR bundle from HL7→FHIR Transform (bundle mode)
Validate a standalone FHIR resource from an API enrichment step (resource mode)
Validate required fields per resource type (14 types with hardcoded rules)
Check internal bundle references point to existing resources (bundle mode)
Enforce specific resource types must be present (e.g., Patient + Encounter)
Full R4 schema validation using 146 JSON schema definitions (strict mode)
Stop the pipeline on validation failure (fail_on_error: true)

parameters.name: validation_level
parameters.description: "basic" (resourceType + id only), "standard" (+ required fields + references), "strict" (+ full R4 JSON schema). Default: "standard".

parameters.name: required_resources
parameters.description: FHIR resource types that must be present. In bundle mode, checks all entries. In resource mode, checks the single resource matches. Example: ["Patient", "Encounter"].

parameters.name: validate_references
parameters.description: Check that reference fields resolve to existing resources (by fullUrl or ResourceType/id). Most useful in bundle mode where references can be cross-checked. Default: true.

parameters.name: validate_required_fields
parameters.description: Check FHIR-spec-required fields per resource type (e.g., Encounter must have status and class, Observation must have status and code). Default: true.

parameters.name: fail_on_error
parameters.description: When true, the pipeline stops if any validation error is found. When false, errors are reported in step output but the pipeline continues. Default: false.

validationTypes.description: Minimal structural check. Only verifies that each resource in the bundle has a resourceType and id.
validationTypes.usedFor: Quick sanity check, development/debugging, high-throughput pipelines where speed matters.

validationTypes.description: Checks required fields per resource type using hardcoded rules for 14 common FHIR resource types. Also validates that internal bundle references point to existing resources.
validationTypes.usedFor: Production pipelines. Catches common mapping errors like missing Encounter.status or MessageHeader.event.

validationTypes.description: Full R4 JSON schema validation using 146 FHIR resource schema definitions. Validates required fields from the official spec, element data types, and cardinality constraints.
validationTypes.usedFor: Compliance validation, regulatory submissions, interoperability testing.

post.delivery.description: Delivers transformed FHIR resources to target FHIR server or other destinations. Handles retries and error recovery.
useCases: Send FHIR Bundle to healthcare FHIR server
Post individual resources to RESTful FHIR API
Deliver to multiple endpoints (primary + backup)
Archive to object storage (S3, Azure Blob)
Queue for async processing

parameters.name: endpoint
parameters.description: FHIR server URL

parameters.name: resource
parameters.description: Resource type to send (Patient, Bundle, etc.)

parameters.name: retry_count
parameters.description: Number of retry attempts (default: 3)

control.loop.description: Container step that executes nested steps in a loop. Supports three loop types: For Each (iterate over collections like OBX segments), For (repeat N times), and While (condition-based). Child steps are visually nested inside the loop container and execute on each iteration with access to loop variables.
useCases: Process all OBX segments in a lab result message (For Each over enhancedSegments.OBX)
Transform multiple diagnosis codes (For Each over DG1 segments)
Retry failed operations up to N times (For loop with retry logic)
Poll external API until data is ready (While loop with condition check)
Process patient encounters in batch (For Each over encounter list)
Apply transformations to all observations (For Each with nested transform steps)
Generate multiple FHIR resources from repeating HL7 segments

example.description: Process all OBX segments and transform to FHIR Observations

parameters.name: loopType
parameters.description: Type of loop: "foreach" (iterate collection), "for" (repeat N times), "while" (condition-based)

parameters.name: collection
parameters.description: For "foreach": Field path to the array/collection to iterate over. Example: "enhancedSegments.OBX" for all OBX segments.

parameters.name: itemVariable
parameters.description: Variable name for current item. Access as loop.{name} in child steps. Default: "item"

parameters.name: indexVariable
parameters.description: Variable name for current index. Access as loop.{name} in child steps. Default: "index"

parameters.name: iterations
parameters.description: For "for" loops: Number of times to execute the loop body.

parameters.name: condition
parameters.description: For "while" loops: Condition object with field, operator, and value. Loop continues while condition is true.

parameters.name: childStepIds
parameters.description: IDs of steps to execute in the loop body. Steps execute in order for each iteration.

parameters.name: maxIterations
parameters.description: Safety limit to prevent infinite loops. Default: 1000

parameters.name: breakOnError
parameters.description: Stop loop execution if a child step fails. Default: false (continue to next iteration)

parameters.name: continueOnEmpty
parameters.description: Continue pipeline if collection is empty. Default: true

loopVariables.title: Available Loop Variables
loopVariables.description: Variables available inside child steps during loop execution:

variables.name: loop.{itemVariable}
variables.description: Current item being processed (For Each only)

variables.name: loop.isFirst
variables.description: True if this is the first iteration

variables.name: loop.isLast
variables.description: True if this is the last iteration

variables.name: loop.length
variables.description: Total number of items (For Each only)

variables.name: loop.total
variables.description: Total number of iterations (For loop only)

types.name: For Each
types.description: Iterates over each item in a collection
types.useCase: Process all OBX segments, transform multiple diagnosis codes

types.name: For (N times)
types.description: Repeats execution a fixed number of times
types.useCase: Retry operations, batch processing with fixed count

types.name: While
types.description: Continues while a condition is true
types.useCase: Poll until ready, process until quota reached

bestPractices.practice: Always set maxIterations
bestPractices.reason: Prevents infinite loops that could hang the pipeline
bestPractices.example: Set maxIterations to a reasonable value like 100 or 1000 based on expected data size

bestPractices.practice: Use meaningful variable names
bestPractices.reason: Makes child step configuration more readable
bestPractices.example: Use "observation" instead of "item" when iterating OBX segments

bestPractices.practice: Consider breakOnError setting
bestPractices.reason: Decide if one failed iteration should stop all processing
bestPractices.example: Set breakOnError=true for critical data, false for best-effort processing

bestPractices.practice: Handle empty collections
bestPractices.reason: Messages may not always have the expected segments
bestPractices.example: Set continueOnEmpty=true to gracefully handle messages without OBX segments

troubleshooting.issue: Loop not executing any iterations
troubleshooting.cause: Collection path is incorrect or collection is empty
troubleshooting.fix: Verify collection path using the field selector. Check if continueOnEmpty is set correctly.

troubleshooting.issue: Loop stops after max iterations
troubleshooting.cause: maxIterations limit reached
troubleshooting.fix: Increase maxIterations if you expect more items, or check for infinite loop conditions in While loops

troubleshooting.issue: Child steps not receiving loop variables
troubleshooting.cause: Variable names not matching between loop config and child step config
troubleshooting.fix: Ensure itemVariable and indexVariable names match what child steps expect

troubleshooting.issue: While loop runs forever
troubleshooting.cause: Condition never becomes false
troubleshooting.fix: Verify condition field is being updated by child steps. Always have maxIterations as safety limit.

core.mapping.description:
Transforms HL7 v2 messages to FHIR R4 format in two passes:

1. Field mapping — each row in the Visual Mapping tab maps one HL7 field (e.g. PID.5) to one FHIR path (e.g. Patient.name[0].family). Enriched data from upstream steps can be referenced as source fields using the ["step_name"].enriched_data.field syntax.

2. Structural assembly (Assembly tab) — runs automatically after field mapping for message types that need it. For ORU^R01 this converts every OBX segment into a properly structured FHIR Observation (value type dispatch, structured referenceRange, interpretation flags, laboratory category) and links them all to DiagnosticReport.result[]. Each assembly rule can be individually disabled in the Assembly tab if your interface requires custom handling. To extend beyond what the OOB rules produce, add a Script Enrichment step after this one — it receives the fully assembled fhirResources array.
useCases: Convert ADT^A01 (patient admission) to FHIR Patient + Encounter + AllergyIntolerance
Transform ORU^R01 (lab results) to FHIR Observation + DiagnosticReport with OBX value dispatch
Map ORM^O01 (order) to FHIR ServiceRequest
Convert DFT^P03 (billing) to FHIR Claim
Enrich FHIR resources with lookup data from a prior Database Enrichment step
Disable specific assembly rules (e.g. referenceRange parsing) for non-standard interfaces
Add a Script Enrichment step after this one to post-process or extend assembled FHIR resources

Hide noisy or irrelevant fields from a resource type's auto-generated narrative summary (resource.text.div) via the Narrative Fields tab, without touching the field mappings that produce the resource itself

mappings.comment: Use enriched data from database lookup

parameters.name: fhir_version
parameters.description: Target FHIR version. Currently R4 is fully supported.

parameters.name: use_template
parameters.description: Use wizard-configured field mappings (default: true).

parameters.name: mappings
parameters.description: Array of field mappings. Each entry maps one HL7 field or enriched value to one FHIR path.

parameters.name: assembleObservations
parameters.description: Master switch for structural assembly. When false all assembly rules are skipped regardless of individual rule settings. Default: true.

parameters.name: assemblyRules
parameters.description: Per-rule on/off flags for structural assembly. All rules default to true when absent. Set a key to false to disable that specific transform. Keys: collapse_text_obx, obs_value_dispatch, obs_value_unit, obs_code, obs_reference_range, obs_interpretation, obs_status, obs_category, obs_subject, obs_effective, obs_nte_note, dr_result_links, dr_subject, dr_code, dr_status, dr_effective, dr_category.

assemblyRulesDoc.desc: Merge mode — controlled in the "Text Report Merging" card at the top of the Assembly tab. When enabled, consecutive TX/FT OBX segments sharing the same OBX.3 code are joined into one Observation.valueString (the HL7 continuation-segment pattern). Example: a 50-line surgical pathology report sent as OBX|1|TX … OBX|50|TX all with OBX.3=4050097^Surg Path produces one Observation instead of 50. Disable (or restrict to specific services via collapse_text_obx_services) when your discrete lab results also happen to use the same OBX.3 across rows. Examples where merging is correct: AP (Anatomic Pathology), RAD (Radiology), SP (Surgical Path). Examples where merging should be OFF or restricted: CH (Chemistry), MB (Microbiology) — each analyte has a distinct OBX.3.
Dispatches OBX value to the correct FHIR type: NM→valueQuantity (float), CE/CWE→valueCodeableConcept, ST/TX→valueString, TS→valueDateTime.
Populates unit + system on valueQuantity. Normalizes UCUM coding system to http://unitsofmeasure.org.
Builds CodeableConcept from OBX.3. Normalizes LN → http://loinc.org, local codes are preserved with display text.
Parses "3.8-11.0" into structured {low:{value,unit}, high:{value,unit}, text}. Disable if your system uses non-numeric or multi-part ranges.
Maps abnormal flags to FHIR interpretation codes: H→High, L→Low, A→Abnormal, AA→Critical, HH→Critical High, LL→Critical Low, N is ignored.
Maps OBX status code to FHIR: F→final, P→preliminary, C→corrected, W→entered-in-error, X→cancelled.
Adds the standard laboratory category coding (http://terminology.hl7.org/CodeSystem/observation-category | laboratory).
Links Observation.subject → Patient/<id> using the Patient resource already in the output.

Clubs consecutive NTE segments following an OBX into Observation.note[0].text. Multiple NTE lines joined with newlines; blank lines become paragraph breaks. NTE after OBR (before first OBX) goes to DiagnosticReport.note.
Populates DiagnosticReport.result[] with references to all assembled Observations.
Builds CodeableConcept from OBR.4 (ordered test / panel code). Required field in FHIR R4 DiagnosticReport.
Maps OBR result status to FHIR: F→final, P→preliminary, C→corrected, X→cancelled.
Converts OBR.7 observation date/time from HL7 TS to ISO 8601. Preferred over OBX.14 for the report-level timestamp.
Adds the standard LAB category coding (http://terminology.hl7.org/CodeSystem/v2-0074 | LAB).

bestPractices.practice: Use the Narrative Fields tab to control resource.text.div content, not the Visual Mapping tab
bestPractices.reason: Narrative field visibility is stored separately from step.config.mappings — per (interfaceId, messageType), via GET/PATCH /api/fhir/optional-segments — the same config surface the interface wizard's Step 4 panel and this step's cda.to_fhir/fhir.build siblings all share, since a resource built by any of them should narrate consistently.
bestPractices.example: Hiding AllergyIntolerance.criticality from the narrative for one interface: expand it in the Narrative Fields tab and uncheck it — no change to the field mappings that put criticality on the resource in the first place.

troubleshooting.issue: A field I unchecked in the Narrative Fields tab still shows up in resource.text.div
troubleshooting.cause: Narrative field visibility is scoped per (interfaceId, messageType) — resolved from step.config.interface_id/message_type, falling back to the pipeline's own interfaceId/messageType. If those didn't resolve to what you expected when the tab loaded, the save landed on a different scope than the resource you're actually looking at.

parameters.name: connectorType
parameters.description: The listener type. tcp_mllp is the primary HL7 transport (also accepted as tcp_mllp_inbound). See Connector Type Reference section below for all supported types.

parameters.name: config
parameters.description: Connector-specific settings driven by the connector type. See sub-fields below.

parameters.name: config.host
parameters.description: Bind address for TCP/MLLP (default: 0.0.0.0 — all interfaces).

parameters.name: config.port
parameters.description: TCP port to listen on (default: 2575 — standard MLLP port).

parameters.name: config.tls_enabled
parameters.description: Enable TLS 1.2/1.3. Requires tls_cert_file and tls_key_file.

parameters.name: config.max_connections
parameters.description: Maximum simultaneous client connections (default: 100).

parameters.name: config.ack
parameters.description: ACK/NACK configuration for TCP/MLLP Inbound. Controls how the connector acknowledges received HL7 messages.

parameters.name: config.ack.mode
parameters.description: "immediate" — send AA as soon as the message is queued (default). "none" — do not send any ACK (sender must not expect a response).

parameters.name: config.ack.on_error
parameters.description: "suppress" — always send AA even on errors, handle failures internally (default). "nack" — send AE so the sender can retry when the queue is full or a critical error occurs.

parameters.name: config.ack.sending_app
parameters.description: MSH-3 in the generated ACK message (default: "ezHealthKonnect").

parameters.name: config.ack.sending_facility
parameters.description: MSH-4 in the generated ACK message (default: "EHK").

parameters.name: config.ack.text_success
parameters.description: MSA-3 text when sending AA (default: "Message received successfully").

parameters.name: config.ack.text_error
parameters.description: MSA-3 text when sending AE or AR (default: "Message processing error").

parameters.name: config.ack.script
parameters.description: Advanced: JavaScript function that fully overrides ACK logic. Must define buildACK(msg) returning { ackCode, textMessage }. Valid ackCode values: AA, AE, AR. Available on msg: controlID, messageType, sendingApp, sendingFacility, raw, defaultCode, defaultText. Errors fall back to the default ACK.

parameters.name: timeoutMs
parameters.description: Maximum wait time for data fetch in milliseconds (default: 30000). Not used for long-lived TCP listeners.

bestPractices.practice: Error Handling — configure per-step error handling on the connector.inbound step
bestPractices.reason: If the inbound step itself fails (e.g. port already in use, bad config), the pipeline will not start. Setting onError: "suppress" lets the engine log the failure and continue trying to activate other steps.
bestPractices.example: In the step properties, open "Error Handling & Retry" → set On Error = suppress, Default Value = {} to prevent pipeline abort on transient startup failures.

bestPractices.practice: Retry — add retry config for pull-mode connectors (SFTP, S3, DB)
bestPractices.reason: Pull connectors run on a schedule. If the remote server is temporarily unreachable, retry logic can transparently retry 2–3 times within the same poll window before failing.
bestPractices.example: Error Handling & Retry → Enable Retry = on, Max Retries = 3, Delay = 5000 ms, Backoff Multiplier = 2 (exponential: 5s, 10s, 20s).

bestPractices.practice: Error Handling — use onError: nack for TCP/MLLP ACK on critical errors
bestPractices.reason: When a message causes a fatal downstream error (e.g. DB unavailable), sending AE (application error) or AR lets the HL7 sender retry rather than silently dropping the message.
bestPractices.example: ACK tab → On Error = nack. The sender receives AE and can retry after its own retry interval.

bestPractices.practice: ACK mode = none for fire-and-forget senders
bestPractices.reason: Some legacy HL7 systems do not read ACK responses and will block the socket waiting for data that never matters. Setting mode=none closes the send side immediately.
bestPractices.example: ACK tab → ACK Mode = none. No ACK message is sent; the MLLP session ends after receiving the message.

file_parser.description: Parses structured files into an array of records for downstream pipeline steps. Supports CSV, TSV, fixed-width positional (CCLF, NACHA, X12), Excel .xlsx/.xls, Apache Avro, and Apache Parquet. Three source modes: read content from a pipeline field (field), from the server filesystem (local_path), or from a URI stored in a pipeline field — including s3://, https://, and file:// (field_as_path). Includes OOB healthcare templates for common fixed-width formats so no column mapping is needed. Typically placed after an Inbound Connector step, followed by Remove Duplicates and a Loop to process each record.
useCases: Parse a CSV feed received via SFTP — content stored in a pipeline field by the Inbound Connector
Parse a fixed-width CCLF Part A file from a local volume mount using the cclf1 OOB template — no column mapping required
Parse a NACHA ACH payment file using the nacha_entry OOB template
Read a CSV from S3: a prior API step stores the S3 URI in a field, field_as_path fetches and parses it (credentials from interface connectivity config)
Parse an Excel .xlsx spreadsheet received as base64 content in a pipeline field
Parse Apache Avro files from Kafka consumers or data pipelines — column names come from the embedded Avro schema
Parse Apache Parquet exports from data warehouses (Snowflake, BigQuery, Databricks) — supports files up to 500 MB
Batch mode: parse all CCLF files in a directory matching a glob pattern and combine into one record array
Auto-detect format: drop any file and let magic bytes and heuristics determine CSV/TSV/XLSX/Avro/Parquet automatically
Sample a large CSV with maxRecords: 100 — streaming read, only 100 rows loaded into memory regardless of file size

parameters.name: sourceType
parameters.description: Where to read the file from. "field" (default) — raw file content already in a pipeline field (set by an Inbound Connector). "local_path" — read directly from the server/container filesystem; supports glob pattern + batch mode. "field_as_path" — a pipeline field holds a URI that is resolved at runtime: s3://bucket/key (AWS S3, credentials from interface connectivity config), https://... (HTTP GET), file:///... (local filesystem).

parameters.name: sourceField
parameters.description: For sourceType=field: the pipeline field holding raw file content (e.g. "enriched.sftp_content"). For sourceType=field_as_path: the pipeline field holding the URI to resolve (e.g. "enriched.s3_uri").

parameters.name: filePath
parameters.description: For sourceType=local_path: absolute path to the file or directory on the server/container (e.g. "/data/cclf/PARTA.T.ACO.D250101.T000001"). With batchMode=true, this is the base directory and filePattern is the glob.

parameters.name: batchMode
parameters.description: local_path only. When true, processes all files matching filePattern in the filePath directory and returns a combined array of results with per-file record counts. Use for daily batch feeds where an entire directory needs to be processed.

parameters.name: filePattern
parameters.description: Glob filename pattern used in batch mode (e.g. "PARTA*.T.*"). Combined with filePath to produce the full glob. Example: filePath="/data/cclf" + filePattern="PARTA*.T.*" matches all Part A files in the directory.

parameters.name: autoDetect
parameters.description: Enable automatic format detection. Magic bytes are checked first (detects XLSX, XLS, Avro, Parquet from binary headers). Then file extension (for local_path). Then delimiter heuristics (CSV vs TSV). Also auto-infers hasHeader from column name patterns. Overrides fileFormat.

parameters.name: fileFormat
parameters.description: Explicit format: csv, tsv, fixed_width, xlsx, xls, avro, parquet, auto. Binary formats (xlsx, xls, avro, parquet) are auto-detected from magic bytes when sourceType=local_path, overriding whatever is configured. Avro and Parquet derive column names from their embedded schema — hasHeader is ignored for these.

parameters.name: template
parameters.description: OOB template key for fixed-width formats — no manual column mapping needed. Available templates: cclf1 (Part A Claims Header), cclf2 (Part A Revenue), cclf3 (Part A PPS/SNF), cclf4 (Part B Physicians), cclf5 (Part B DME), cclf6 (Part D Drug Events), cclf7 (Beneficiary Demographics), cclf8 (Beneficiary XREF), nacha_entry (ACH Entry Detail), era_835_header (X12 835 Interchange).

parameters.name: columns
parameters.description: Manual column definitions for fixed-width format. Each entry: { name, start, length }. Start is 1-based byte position, length is field width in bytes. Overrides template if both are set.

parameters.name: delimiter
parameters.description: Field separator character for CSV/TSV. Default: comma for CSV, tab for TSV. Ignored for binary formats (xlsx, xls, avro, parquet).

parameters.name: hasHeader
parameters.description: Whether the first row contains column names. Default: true. When false, columns are named col_1, col_2, ... for CSV/TSV. Ignored for Avro and Parquet (schema is embedded).

parameters.name: sheetName
parameters.description: xlsx/xls: Name of the sheet to parse. Leave empty to use the first sheet. Use sheetIndex if the sheet has no name.

parameters.name: sheetIndex
parameters.description: xlsx/xls: 0-based sheet index. Used when sheetName is empty. Default: 0 (first sheet).

parameters.name: contentEncoding
parameters.description: Set to "base64" when binary file content (Excel, Avro, Parquet) was base64-encoded before being stored in a pipeline field. Common when binary data passes through JSON-based APIs or message queues. The executor decodes it before parsing.

parameters.name: trimFields
parameters.description: Trim leading/trailing whitespace from all string values. Default: true. Applies to CSV, TSV, fixed-width, and string fields in Avro/Parquet.

parameters.name: skipRows
parameters.description: Number of rows/records to skip from the top before parsing begins. Useful for files with non-data header rows (e.g. report title, generation date). For Avro/Parquet: skips that many records in the stream.

parameters.name: maxRecords
parameters.description: Maximum records to parse (0 = unlimited). For CSV/TSV: uses streaming when set — only maxRecords rows are read from the file, making it O(maxRecords) memory regardless of file size. Ideal for sampling large files. For Avro/Parquet: stops reading after maxRecords records.

parameters.name: maxFileSizeMB
parameters.description: File size limit in MB for local_path and file:// sources (0 = default 100 MB, hard cap 500 MB). The file size is checked via stat() before reading — oversized files are rejected immediately with a descriptive error. Use maxRecords to sample files larger than the limit.

parameters.name: interface_id
parameters.description: Required when sourceType=field_as_path and the URI is an s3:// address. Identifies which interface connectivity config to look up for AWS credentials (access key ID, secret access key, region). Credentials are AES-256-GCM decrypted at runtime — never stored in plaintext in the step config.

remove_duplicates.description:
Removes duplicate records from an array field using configurable key fields and merge strategies. Supports full-record hashing (no key fields needed), multi-field composite keys, three merge strategies, case-insensitive matching, and flexible handling of records with missing keys.

Source arrays come from prior steps via the steps.{namespace}.step_output path — for example a File Parser step produces steps.{ns}.step_output.records, a Database Enrichment step produces steps.{ns}.step_output.rows. Use the "Detect fields" button in the UI to auto-populate key field candidates.
useCases: Remove duplicate patient rows parsed from a CSV or CCLF file (key: patient_mrn)
Dedup FHIR bundle entries by resource.id before loading into a FHIR server
Dedup claims rows from an 835/837 file by claim_id + line_num
Dedup HL7 OBX observations by test_code + observation_date within one message
Merge partial records — keep first occurrence, backfill missing fields from later duplicates (strategy: merge)
Drop records with null patient_id (nullKeyBehavior: remove) before FHIR mapping
Deduplicate API enrichment results that return the same record multiple times

examples.label: Dedup CSV records by patient ID (keep first)
Dedup claims by claim ID + line number (keep last = most recent correction)
Merge partial lab records — backfill missing fields from later duplicates
Dedup database rows, write to new field (preserve original)
Full-record strict dedup — no key fields (every field must match)

parameters.name: sourceField
parameters.description: Dot-path to the array to deduplicate. Must point to an array produced by a prior step — File Parser: steps.{ns}.step_output.records; Database Enrichment: steps.{ns}.step_output.rows; Script Enrichment: steps.{ns}.step_output.{yourField}. Use the Source Step picker in the UI to auto-build this path.

parameters.name: keyFields
parameters.description: Field names within each record that form the unique key. Supports dot-paths for nested fields (e.g. "patient.id"). Leave empty to hash the entire record — every field must match for a record to count as a duplicate. Use the "Detect fields" button to auto-populate from upstream step output.

parameters.name: strategy
parameters.description: "first" (default) — keep the earliest occurrence, discard all later duplicates. "last" — keep the most recent occurrence (useful when later records are corrections). "merge" — keep the first record and non-destructively backfill any absent fields from later records.

parameters.name: caseSensitive
parameters.description: When false, key field values are lowercased before hashing so "SMITH" = "smith". Default: true.

parameters.name: nullKeyBehavior
parameters.description: "group" (default) — records with null/absent key fields share one dedup bucket. "keep" — records with missing keys bypass dedup and are always kept. "remove" — records with null or absent key fields are dropped entirely.

parameters.name: outputField
parameters.description: Write the deduplicated array to this field instead of updating sourceField in-place. Leave empty to update the source array directly. Example: "deduped_patients" — downstream steps access it as steps.{thisStep}.step_output.result_path.

parameters.name: previewLimit
parameters.description: Maximum records to include in the step_output.records preview (default 100, max 1000). The full deduplicated array is always written to outputField/sourceField regardless of this setting.

stepOutput.description: The full deduplicated array is written to outputField (or sourceField when outputField is blank). The following variables are also available in downstream steps via steps.{ns}.step_output:

fields.name: result_path
fields.description: Dot-path where the full deduplicated array was written (use this in downstream sourceField configs)

fields.name: records

fields.name: records_truncated
fields.description: true when the full result has more rows than the preview limit

fields.name: original_count
fields.description: Total records in the source array before dedup

fields.name: dedup_count
fields.description: Records in the deduplicated output

fields.name: removed_count
fields.description: Duplicate records discarded

fields.name: null_key_kept
fields.description: Records with missing keys that were kept (nullKeyBehavior=keep)

fields.name: null_key_removed
fields.description: Records with missing keys that were dropped (nullKeyBehavior=remove)

data_masking.description:
Masks or anonymizes sensitive PHI/PII fields for HIPAA compliance. Applies ordered masking rules to individual fields using six strategies:

  • mask — replace every character with maskChar (default *)
  • redact — replace with [REDACTED]
  • partial — reveal first N and/or last N characters, mask the middle
  • hash — SHA-256 deterministic 16-char hex (same salt = same output = join-safe de-ID)
  • tokenize — non-reversible TOK-{12hex} token
  • substitute — replace with realistic fake data (name, SSN, phone, email, date, address, or custom fixed value)

Field paths are format-agnostic — any of these work:
  • HL7 v2:  PID.5, PID.19, MSH.9.1
  • FHIR R4: steps.hl7_fhir_transform.step_output.fhir_bundle.entry[0].resource.patient.name[0].family
    (entry index is auto-resolved — if the Patient is at entry[1], it will be found automatically)
  • Cross-step JSON: steps.api_enrichment.step_output.email
  • CSV / DB records: steps.file_parser.step_output.records[0].ssn
    (index [0] is auto-searched across all records in the array)

Enable "Mask All PHI" to instantly apply pre-configured HIPAA Safe Harbor rules for the selected format (HL7 v2: 23 rules / FHIR R4: 20 rules / JSON: 18 rules). Custom rules run after.

Step output is available downstream via steps.{namespace}.step_output.*

Hash SSN (PID.19) for de-identification while keeping cross-dataset join capability
Partial-mask phone — keep last 4 digits: 555-867-5309 → ***-***-5309 (preserveFormat)
Substitute patient name with realistic fake name for synthetic test data generation

Use preserveFormat with partial to keep SSN dashes: 123-45-6789 → ***-**-6789

parameters.name: rules
parameters.description: Ordered list of field masking rules. Each rule specifies a field path and strategy. Rules run in sequence. If multiple rules match the same field, the last one applied wins.

parameters.name: rules[].field
parameters.description:
Field path to mask. Supports all formats:
  HL7 v2: PID.5, PID.19, MSH.9.1, PID.5.1
  FHIR R4: steps.{step}.step_output.fhir_bundle.entry[0].resource.patient.name[0].family
    (entry[N] index is auto-searched if the field is not found at index N)
  Cross-step JSON: steps.{step}.step_output.email
  CSV / DB records: steps.{step}.step_output.records[0].field_name
    (array index is auto-searched across all records)
  Generic JSON: data.patient.ssn, message.payload.name

parameters.name: rules[].strategy
parameters.description:
Masking strategy:
  "mask"       — replace all chars with maskChar (default *). Example: John → ****
  "redact"     — replace with [REDACTED]. Example: John → [REDACTED]
  "partial"    — keep keepFirst chars at start and keepLast chars at end, mask middle.
                 Example: 555-867-5309 with keepLast=4 → 555-867-****
                 Set preserveFormat=true to also keep non-digit separators in place.
  "hash"       — SHA-256 of (hashSalt + value), returns first 16 hex chars.
                 Deterministic: same input + same salt = same output (join-safe de-ID).
  "tokenize"   — non-reversible token: TOK-{12 hex chars}. Each unique value gets a unique token.
  "substitute" — replace with realistic fake data. Set substituteType to control output:
                 name, ssn (9XX-XX-XXXX ITIN range), phone ((555) XXX-XXXX),
                 email (test.{hex}@example-test.com), date (preserves year),
                 address (1000-9999 fictional street), custom (fixed substituteValue).
                 All substitute values are deterministic — same input = same fake output.

parameters.name: rules[].substituteType
parameters.description: Category of fake data to generate (substitute strategy only). Options: name, ssn, phone, email, date, address, custom. All types produce values that are clearly non-real and safe for test environments.

parameters.name: rules[].substituteValue
parameters.description: Fixed replacement string used when substituteType is "custom". Example: substituteValue: "[TEST PATIENT]". The same value is used for every field match.

parameters.name: rules[].maskChar
parameters.description: Replacement character for mask and partial strategies. Default: *.

parameters.name: rules[].keepFirst
parameters.description: Characters to reveal at the start of the value (partial strategy). Default: 0.

parameters.name: rules[].keepLast
parameters.description: Characters to reveal at the end of the value (partial strategy). Default: 4.

parameters.name: rules[].hashSalt
parameters.description: Salt prepended before SHA-256 hashing (hash strategy). Default: "ezHealthKonnect". Use the same salt across environments to preserve cross-dataset join capability on hashed values.

parameters.name: rules[].pattern
parameters.description: Optional regex. When set, only substrings matching the pattern are masked — non-matching characters are preserved. Example: \d{4} on "Acct 1234-5678" masks only the digits.

parameters.name: maskAllPHI
parameters.description:
When true, prepends format-specific HIPAA Safe Harbor rules before any custom rules:
  HL7 v2 (23 rules): Names (PID.5/6, NK1.2, GT1.3), Geographic (PID.11.x), Dates (PID.7/29, PV1.44/45),
    Phone/Fax (PID.13/14), Email (PID.13.4), SSN (PID.19 hash), MRN (PID.3 partial),
    Insurance (IN1.49/2), Account (PID.18), License (PID.20 hash), Device ID (OBX.18 hash), Other IDs (PID.2/4)
  FHIR R4 (20 rules): Patient.name, Patient.address, Patient.birthDate, Patient.telecom,
    Patient.identifier, Encounter.period, Coverage, Account, Practitioner, Device
  JSON (18 rules): patient.name/firstName/lastName, patient.dateOfBirth/dob, patient.ssn,
    patient.phone/fax, patient.email, patient.mrn, patient.address, patient.zipCode, patient.insuranceId
Custom rules still apply after the auto-PHI rules.

parameters.name: maskAllPHIFormat
parameters.description: Format for auto-PHI rules when maskAllPHI is true. Options: "hl7v2" (default), "fhir", "json". Set to "fhir" when masking data after an HL7→FHIR transform step, or "json" when masking generic JSON patient records from a DB or CSV source.

parameters.name: preserveFormat
parameters.description: For partial strategy: mask digit characters only and keep non-digit separators in place. Example: 555-867-5309 with keepLast=4 → ***-***-5309. keepFirst/keepLast count only digits — separators are never counted or masked.

stepOutput.description: Reference these in downstream steps via steps.{namespace}.step_output.*

fields.name: masked_count
fields.description: Number of fields successfully masked. A field not found in the message is not counted.

fields.name: masked_fields
fields.description: Ordered list of resolved field paths that were masked (may differ from the configured path when entry index was auto-resolved).

fields.name: total_rules
fields.description: Total rules evaluated including maskAllPHI auto-rules.

payload.builder.description:
Constructs the final outbound wire payload from pipeline data — the last transform step before an Outbound Connector. Four modes:

  • Simple (pass_through) — resolve one pipeline variable and serialize it. Smart default when source_path is blank: tries fhirBundle, then fhir_bundle, then message. If the resolved value is already a string (e.g. a raw HL7 string) it is sent as-is, unserialized.
  • Template — {{ variable.path }} placeholder substitution in a hand-written template string (JSON, HL7, or any text). Unresolved variables are replaced with an empty string rather than failing the step.
  • Field Builder — build an output object from an ordered list of target-path -> source mappings (literal value or field_ref pipeline path).
  • FHIR Bundle — resolve one or more pipeline paths, each expected to hold a FHIR resource (or an array of them), and wrap them into a FHIR R4 Bundle.

FHIR Bundle mode does three things automatically so the caller never has to: (1) generates resource.text.div narrative for any resource that does not already have one, honoring the same per-interface narrative_fields config an hl7_fhir_transform-sourced resource would use; (2) assigns every entry a urn:uuid: fullUrl and rewrites every "ResourceType/id" reference in every resource to match, via the same AssembleEntries logic the CDA/FHIR document assembler uses; (3) adds entry.request {method, url} blocks automatically for transaction/batch bundles (PUT when the resource has an id, POST otherwise) — includeRequest only needs to be set explicitly for a collection/document bundle that should still carry request blocks.

Step output is written to _stepOutput and also exposed at the top level (payload, content_type) so an Outbound Connector's contentField="payload" works without extra config.
useCases: Simple mode: send the fhirBundle produced by an hl7_fhir_transform/core.mapping step straight to an HTTP FHIR outbound connector
Simple mode: forward the raw HL7 message unchanged to a TCP/MLLP outbound connector (source_path="message", value is already a string)
Template mode: build a custom JSON payload for a third-party REST API, inlining values like {{ PID.5.1 }} or {{ steps.enrich.step_output.mrn }}
Field Builder mode: assemble a flat JSON object for a billing system from several different upstream steps, without writing a script
FHIR Bundle mode: assemble a transaction Bundle from a Patient + Encounter + Observation built by earlier fhir.build/cda.to_fhir steps and POST it to a FHIR server
FHIR Bundle mode: build a document Bundle (Composition first) for a CDA-derived FHIR Document
FHIR Bundle mode: combine resources produced by more than one upstream branch (e.g. a Patient from cda.to_fhir plus Observations from a separate hl7 branch) into one outbound Bundle

examples.label: Simple — pass through the HL7->FHIR transform output as FHIR R4
Simple — forward the raw inbound HL7 message unchanged
Template — custom JSON for a third-party API
Field Builder — flat JSON object from mixed literal + field sources
FHIR Bundle — collection of two resources, no request blocks

parameters.name: mode
parameters.description: Which build strategy to use. Default: pass_through. Determines which of the other config keys apply.

parameters.name: source_path
parameters.description: pass_through only. Pipeline variable to resolve and send as the payload. Leave blank for the smart default: tries fhirBundle, then fhir_bundle, then message, in that order. A string value (e.g. raw HL7) is sent as-is; any other value is serialized to output_format.

parameters.name: template
parameters.description: template mode only. A string containing {{ variable.path }} placeholders. Each placeholder is resolved against the pipeline data (format-agnostic — HL7 field paths, FHIR paths, or plain JSON dot-paths all work) and substituted; objects/arrays are JSON-serialized, everything else is stringified. Unresolved placeholders become "".

parameters.name: field_mappings
parameters.description: field_builder mode only. Ordered list of output fields. target is a dot-path in the output object (array-index notation like entry[0] is stripped and treated as a plain key in v1). source_type is "literal" (uses value) or "field_ref" (resolves source as a pipeline path).

parameters.name: fhirBundle.bundleType
parameters.description: fhir_bundle mode only. Default: collection. transaction/batch always get entry.request blocks regardless of includeRequest. document expects the first resolved resource to be a Composition. Bundle.total is never set for these four types (only applies to searchset/history, which this step does not produce).

parameters.name: fhirBundle.resourcePaths
parameters.description: fhir_bundle mode only. Ordered pipeline variable paths, each resolving to a FHIR resource map (or a JSON string containing one). A path that resolves to nil or a non-resource value is skipped with a warning rather than failing the whole step; at least one resource must resolve or the step errors.

parameters.name: fhirBundle.bundleId
parameters.description: fhir_bundle mode only. Optional Bundle.id. Auto-generated ("bundle-<nanoseconds>") when left blank.

parameters.name: fhirBundle.includeRequest
parameters.description: fhir_bundle mode only. Adds entry.request {method, url} to every entry — PUT ResourceType/id when the resource has an id, otherwise POST ResourceType (with ifNoneExist for batch bundles). Forced true automatically for transaction/batch bundleType; only needs to be set explicitly for collection/document.

parameters.name: output_format
parameters.description: pass_through/template/field_builder modes. Controls serialization and the default Content-Type header (application/fhir+json, application/hl7-v2, application/json, text/csv respectively). Ignored by fhir_bundle mode, which always emits application/fhir+json.

parameters.name: content_type
parameters.description: Explicit MIME type override. When set, replaces the default derived from output_format for every mode except fhir_bundle.

stepOutput.description: Available downstream via steps.{namespace}.step_output.*, and also exposed at the top level as payload / content_type so an Outbound Connector's default contentField="payload" works without extra configuration.

fields.name: payload
fields.description: The built wire-format payload string, ready to send

fields.name: content_type
fields.description: MIME type to use for the outbound request/message

fields.name: payload_size
fields.description: Size of payload in bytes

fields.name: output_format
fields.description: The output_format this step was configured with

fields.name: error
fields.description: Present only when the step failed — payload is empty in that case
